analysis:
The only change in this file is one added line, head line 251 in requireNativeMiMoPublication: `if let refusal = addonHoldLoadRefusal(for: modelID) { throw refusal }`. It sits after the process-work, shutdown, lifecycle and ownership guards and before throwIfRetiring and load.recheck. This adds a check tied to the TB-012 / T-059 / A-018 add-on hold, so a native MiMo cold load is refused while the local add-on hold is active. It is a fail-closed refusal that narrows what loads can do. It does not weaken any existing guard, add a bypass, or expose data.

The function is called from several points in prepareNativeMiMoSlot and from publishNativeMiMoCandidate. A thrown refusal therefore reaches performNativeMiMoSlotLoad's catch block. That block revokes the load, joins the owned tasks, runs retireNativeMiMoOwner and releases the reslice gate. Unless the error is a CancellationError, the catch rethrows a generic message. The exception is a failed retirement, which keeps its own pending or process-restart message. SDK or refusal details are not reflected onto public surfaces. The error type is unknown, but if it is not a refusal subtype of MiMoV26NativeTransactionError, it takes the normal teardown path. This is the safe path.

Denial of service by a same-UID local process holding the provider out of routing is the T-059 residual and is described by that threat. This change does not make it worse.

Not visible in the supplied evidence: the implementation of addonHoldLoadRefusal (its signature, whether it is synchronous and actor-isolated, and how it reads the hold state). Also not visible: whether the hold is checked at other load paths, such as the generic loader, and the coordinator's handling of the busy fields. These need confirming in the integration pass. Base and head are otherwise identical, so no other regression was identified.
